entries.subject: Ahlers et al. (2020) gravity-darkened fit to KELT-9b's TESS transit
entries.finding: Sets the flattening (equator 1.089 times the pole), the gravity-darkening exponent and the spin axis (i* 52 degrees in the paper's convention, lambda -88 degrees). The Roche-von Zeipel shading from those numbers puts the equator about 500 K below the pole, where the paper's text says 800 to 1,000 K and a 38 percent brightness contrast.

entries.subject: Disc-resolved images or interferometric imaging of KELT-9
entries.finding: The disc is about 0.1 mas across at 207 pc, far below any interferometer's resolution; no image exists. The surface pattern shown is the transit fit's, not an image.
entries.revisitWhen: A reconstructed image of the star's surface is published.

entries.subject: Stephan et al. (2022) joint fit of KELT-9b's nodal precession with Doppler tomography and TESS
entries.finding: A later fit of the spin geometry that uses Ahlers et al. as a prior in one of its runs. The package keeps the single self-consistent TESS fit that also gives the flattening and the gravity-darkening exponent.
entries.revisitWhen: A single paper gives flattening, gravity darkening and spin axis more precisely than Ahlers et al. (2020).
